verified_facts.text: Longitude 131 has views direct to Uluru and across the desert to Kata Tjuta.
verified_facts.excerpt: With views direct to Uluru and across the desert to Kata Tjuta

verified_facts.text: The lodge sits on privately owned land surrounded by Katiti Aboriginal Land and the dual World Heritage listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.
verified_facts.excerpt: Longitude 131° is situated on 23,800 square metres of privately owned land and is surrounded by Katiti Aboriginal Land and the dual World Heritage listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.

verified_facts.text: Guests stay in tented pavilions among the red dunes, with floor-to-ceiling glass framing the desert light.
verified_facts.excerpt: Floor-to-ceiling glass frames the ever-changing light of the desert, while custom furnishings and First Nations artworks layer each space with story and warmth.

verified_facts.text: Each luxury tent offers views to Uluru from the end of the bed.
verified_facts.excerpt: fifteen luxury tents at Longitude 131° each offer views to Uluru – from the end of the bed!

verified_facts.text: Longitude 131 first opened in 2002, with its safari-style tents around a central Dune House designed by Australian architect Philip Cox.
verified_facts.excerpt: Longitude 131° first opened to global acclaim in 2002, with its gathering of safari-style guest tents around a central Dune House the creation of leading Australian architect Philip Cox.

verified_facts.text: The lodge's sustainable design includes renewable energies and the ability to be dismantled and removed entirely.
verified_facts.excerpt: the lodge’s sustainable design includes renewable energies and the ability to be dismantled and removed entirely, restoring the rolling red sand dunes to their original state.

verified_facts.text: The Dune Top has a help-yourself bar, outdoor lounges and a plunge spa with views to both Uluru and Kata Tjuta.
verified_facts.excerpt: the Dune Top is an intimate space comprising a help-yourself bar, outdoor lounges and plunge spa with views to both World Heritage-listed natural icons Uluru and Kata Tjuta.

verified_facts.text: Spa Kinara is inspired by the design of the wiltja, the traditional shelter of the local Anangu people.
verified_facts.excerpt: Spa Kinara is inspired by the clever design of the _wiltja,_ the traditional shelter of the region’s Indigenous Anangu people.

verified_facts.text: Spa Kinara uses irmangka-irmangka, or Scented Emu Bush, a bush medicine used by Aboriginal healers, in many treatments.
verified_facts.excerpt: irmangka-irmangka is also known as Scented Emu Bush and is used in many treatments at Spa Kinara.

verified_facts.text: Spa Kinara is reserved exclusively for in-house guests.
verified_facts.excerpt: Spa Kinara is reserved exclusively for in-house guests.

verified_facts.text: Signature experiences are included in the tariff and run on a shared basis with fellow guests at scheduled times.
verified_facts.excerpt: These experiences are included in the tariff and are provided on an intimate shared basis with fellow guests at scheduled times.

verified_facts.text: Signature experiences include a guided sunrise expedition to Kata Tjuta and Walpa Gorge.
verified_facts.excerpt: Embark on a guided sunrise expedition to Kata Tjuta and Walpa Gorge, including morning tea and a visit to the Cultural Centre.

verified_facts.text: Bruce Munro's Field of Light installation is one of the signature experiences.
verified_facts.excerpt: Artist Bruce Munro’s Field of Light installation of 50,000 bud-like stems that bloom and appear to sway as darkness descends over Australia’s spiritual heartland.

verified_facts.text: Dining combines premium produce from around Australia with bush ingredients.
verified_facts.excerpt: The finest premium produce is delivered to the Red Centre and combined with bush ingredients to offer guests a unique taste of Australia.

verified_facts.text: The lodge runs artists-in-residence visits with Ernabella Arts, where guests can watch Anangu artists paint with views of Uluru and Kata Tjuta.
verified_facts.excerpt: During these visits, guests are invited to observe the creative process, gaining rare insight into the artists’ practice as each vibrant piece comes to life.

verified_facts.text: Helicopter flights lift off from the lodge's helipad at additional charge.
verified_facts.excerpt: Take a Red Centre adventure to new heights, lifting off from the lodge’s helipad on a scenic helicopter flight.

verified_facts.text: Longitude 131 welcomes children ten years and over.
verified_facts.excerpt: Longitude 131° welcomes children ten years and over.

verified_facts.text: Ayers Rock Airport is three hours by air from most Australian capital cities.
verified_facts.excerpt: The main port, Ayers Rock Airport is three hours’ travel by air from most Australian capital cities.

verified_facts.text: The lodge does not handle reservations; bookings go through the Beckons reservations team.
verified_facts.excerpt: Please note, the lodge does not handle general inquiries or reservations.

verified_facts.text: The in-tent bar is included in the stay.
verified_facts.excerpt: A stay at Longitude 131° is generously all-inclusive, even down to the in-tent bar.

verified_facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler places the elevated tents on the edge of Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guests gaze upon "the magical Ayers Rock" from "luxurious elevated tents" on the edge of Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, a perfect-scoring location.

verified_facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler notes the pool is a bit petite.
verified_facts.excerpt: "The pool is a bit petite, but it’s a small price to pay for the overall experience."
